objects.name: Emerald Isle
objects.description: A lush green planet teeming with flora, featuring cascading waterfalls and drifting clouds.
scientificFacts: Planets with high oxygen content and dense vegetation often reflect green wavelengths intensely.
A strong magnetic field is required to protect such biospheres from solar winds.
objects.lore: The Emerald Isle was one of the first worlds seeded by the Architect to test the viability of organic life in this sector.
objects.interestingFacts: It rains upward near the primary waterfall due to localized gravity anomalies.

objects.name: Forge Planet
objects.description: A molten world dominated by a massive supervolcano and glowing lava rivers.
scientificFacts: Volcanic worlds are typically very young or orbit a gas giant, enduring extreme tidal heating.
Lava rivers indicate a very thin crust and high internal radiogenic heating.
objects.lore: The Forge is the Architect's cosmic foundry, where heavy elements and glowing project crystals are forged in the fires of creation.
objects.interestingFacts: The project crystals scattered here contain pure data compressed into physical form.

objects.name: Ocean World
objects.description: A deep blue water world inhabited by glowing jellyfish and swimming whales.
scientificFacts: Ocean worlds, or hycean planets, are prime candidates for finding extraterrestrial marine life.
Bioluminescence is common in deep-sea creatures to attract prey or communicate.
objects.lore: A sanctuary of knowledge, where the Architect's memories swim like whales beneath the waves.
objects.interestingFacts: The floating skill bubbles are actual concentrated pockets of technical knowledge.

objects.name: Crystal Moon
objects.description: A jagged icy moon wrapped in a cracked crust, enveloped in a falling snowstorm and a multi-colored Aurora.
scientificFacts: Auroras are caused by the interaction of solar wind with a strong magnetic field and atmospheric gases.
Ice moons often hide subsurface oceans heated by tidal friction.
objects.lore: The crystal spires hold the frozen echoes of past civilizations that the Architect attempted to save.
objects.interestingFacts: The snow here falls upward during certain orbital alignments.

objects.name: Singularity
objects.description: A supermassive gravitational distortion with a swirling accretion disk.
scientificFacts: A black hole's gravity is so strong that not even light can escape its event horizon.
The bright ring is the accretion disk—superheated gas swirling inward at relativistic speeds.
objects.lore: The gateway to the Architect's personal domain. Only those who master the chaos of code can pass through.
objects.interestingFacts: Time slows down the closer you get to it.
suggestedQuestions: What happens beyond the event horizon?

objects.name: Comet Alpha
objects.description: A fast-moving icy body leaving a bright tail as it travels through the system.
scientificFacts: Comet tails are formed by solar radiation vaporizing the comet's icy nucleus.
The tail always points away from the primary star, regardless of the comet's direction of travel.
objects.lore: Comet Alpha is an ancient messenger carrying primordial stardust from the dawn of this universe.
objects.interestingFacts: Its orbit takes exactly 1,000 years to complete.
suggestedQuestions: What is the tail made of?

objects.name: Comet Beta
objects.description: A slow-drifting comet from the outer edges of the cosmic void.
scientificFacts: Short-period comets originate from the Kuiper Belt, while long-period ones come from the Oort Cloud.
objects.lore: Beta is a stray fragment of a destroyed world, preserved in ice.
objects.interestingFacts: It carries traces of unknown elements.

objects.name: Comet Gamma
objects.description: A highly volatile comet passing perilously close to the central core.
scientificFacts: Sun-grazing comets often break apart due to intense tidal forces and solar heat.
objects.lore: Gamma glows with the fury of a forgotten star's core.
objects.interestingFacts: It is visibly outgassing heavily on its sunward side.

objects.name: Pulsar Alpha
objects.description: A rapidly rotating neutron star emitting intense beams of electromagnetic radiation.
scientificFacts: Pulsars are the incredibly dense remnants of massive stars that collapsed in a supernova.
Their rotation can be so precise they rival atomic clocks.
objects.lore: The Architect uses Pulsar Alpha as a cosmic lighthouse to guide stray matter back into the sector.
objects.interestingFacts: It completes one full rotation every 1.5 milliseconds.
suggestedQuestions: How heavy is a teaspoon of a pulsar?

objects.name: Quasar Prime
objects.description: An extremely luminous active galactic nucleus powered by a supermassive black hole.
scientificFacts: Quasars can outshine entire galaxies containing hundreds of billions of stars.
The energy jets are ejected at nearly the speed of light.
objects.lore: Quasar Prime powers the entire Architect of Worlds simulation engine.
objects.interestingFacts: Its light has been traveling for 12 billion years to reach us.
suggestedQuestions: Are those jets made of fire?

objects.name: Ancient Ruins
objects.description: Drifting monolithic structures inscribed with glowing green runes.
scientificFacts: No known natural process creates perfect monolithic rectangular structures in deep space.
objects.lore: These are the shattered fragments of the very first code ever written by the Architect.
objects.interestingFacts: The runes pulse in rhythm with the user's heartbeat.
